subject: Partner localization & data residency: risk/gap analysis for EU/APAC SIs
messages:
From: Nihal Reddy <nihal@tamarind-llc.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood-inference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 15:14:00 +0200
Subject: Request: residency constraints matrix for potential SI deployments (EU/APAC)

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks again for the intro last week. Tamarind is evaluating a couple of SI partners in France and Japan to run a regional POC for an internal knowledge base use case. Before we lock partners, procurement is asking for a simple matrix that shows where each partner can or cannot satisfy local data residency and access-control constraints (in-country storage, customer-managed KMS, personnel locality for support, audit log retention, and cross-border transfer restrictions).

Can Redwood help by filling a partner-facing template (or confirm what you need from us) so we can show procurement and legal the gaps? The timeline is tight — procurement wants a summary for the July 12 vendor meeting.

Attachments: tamarind-requirements-brief.pdf

Cheers,
Nihal Reddy
Head of Cloud Architecture — Tamarind LLC
nihal@tamarind-llc.com
+44 7700 900123

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood-inference.com>
To: Nihal Reddy <nihal@tamarind-llc.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood-inference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:05:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: residency constraints matrix for potential SI deployments (EU/APAC)

Hi Nihal —

Appreciate the note and timeline. We have a concise template the Partnerships and Compliance teams use to map SI capabilities to customer residency asks. I attached an editable CSV (redwood-partner-residency-draft.csv) with the columns we typically populate: partner, country coverage, in-country storage (yes/no), KMS options (managed/customer), personnel access controls, third-party subprocessors, SOC2 / ISO attestations, audit log retention, and any contractual addenda required.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll populate the sheet for the three candidate SIs we’ve pre-screened (Kenji / Nearshore / local reseller) with our current notes by EOD tomorrow.
- Soojin, can you add partner marketplace/contract constraints (catalog listing, pricing tiers)?
- Diego, can you run a quick signal check with Engineering on whether our Hosted API variant can support customer-managed KMS in those regions without Private deployment? If not, flag as "requires private".
- Nihal — if you can share a prioritized list of the residency items (which items are blockers vs nice-to-have), that will help us prioritize the POC scoping.

I’ll also add a short risk column for each gap (regulatory, technical, contractual) and suggested mitigations.

Attachments: redwood-partner-residency-draft.csv

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Partner Lead | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood-inference.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood-inference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Nihal Reddy <nihal@tamarind-llc.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:42:00 +09:00
Subject: Re: Request: residency constraints matrix for potential SI deployments (EU/APAC)

Thanks — I added three practical columns to the draft and left inline comments:
1) Market enablement required (local legal addendum / procurement playbook / standard SOW)
2) Marketplace listing status (self-serve / partner-managed / not listed)
3) Typical lead time to get KMS/customer-key integrated (estimates in days)

Quick notes on partners:
- Kenji Sato (JP Integrators): strong on in-country ops and can host customer-managed KMS if we can ship an on-prem agent or private connector; typically requests a Platform Addendum and local DPA clause.
- Nearshore Consulting (Claire): good SOC2 hygiene; in France they still push for explicit in-country copy retention unless we can demonstrate PSA-level access controls.
- Tamarind (Nihal): single-tenant POC preferred by their security team — they want explicit audit-log retention policies and proof-of-chain for key rotations.

I’ll flag marketplace blockers and add the owner column for follow-ups. Marissa — can you check with Solutions Eng about whether we can provide an auditable key-rotation log for the Hosted API or if that is Private-only?

Attachment: rdw-si-risk-gap-notes.txt

- Soojin
Channel Partnerships | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood-inference.com
From: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@nearshore-consulting.fr>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Nihal Reddy <nihal@tamarind-llc.com>, Kenji Sato <ksato@jp-integrators.co.jp>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 11:02:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: residency constraints matrix for potential SI deployments (EU/APAC)

Merci — this template is exactly what our procurement teams will use. A few clarifications from the SI side:

> "in-country storage" — we can store encrypted backups in-country but need explicit contract language for cross-border restore (France -> EU region only).
> "customer-managed KMS" — Nearshore can integrate with customer KMS for keys at rest but requires a 3–4 week engineering window and an SOW line item.
> "personnel access" — we operate with role-based access and 24/7 monitored jump-hosts; we will provide a short attestation for local staff access controls.

I attached a short SOW stub summarizing the timelines (tamarind-sow-stub.pdf). We can aim to return the completed matrix by July 6 if Redwood fills the initial partner columns.

Action items for Redwood (per our procurement/legal):
- Confirm whether Hosted API can be configured with customer-managed keys or whether Private is required (Diego/Engineering).
- Provide a short template addendum for in-country backup clauses (Legal / Marissa).
- Populate the matrix for the three named SIs and mark risk mitigations we can offer (canary deployments, region fallback, encryption in transit at every hop).

Happy to hop on a short call next week to finalize.

Best,
Claire Dubois
Head of Partnerships, Nearshore Consulting
claire.dubois@nearshore-consulting.fr
+33 6 12 34 56 78
